# Transaction Data Table Accessibility Design & Testing Plan > **For Claude:** Use a11y-planner protocol. Review with a11y-critic after implementation. > **Compliance target:** WCAG 2.2 AA > **Users who need accessibility:** Screen reader users (NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver), keyboard-only users, low vision users > **Assistive technologies:** NVDA (Windows), JAWS (Windows), VoiceOver (macOS), keyboard-only navigation **Feature:** Sortable, paginated data table with per-row action menus in a financial reporting dashboard **Risk Level:** High (complex interactions, multiple dynamic states, known accessibility risk flag) **Component/Page Type:** DataTable component with sort controls, pagination, and inline dropdown menus --- ## Scope & Context This plan covers the accessibility design and testing strategy for a React-based data table displaying 50 rows per page of transaction records. The component includes sortable column headers (`aria-sort`), paginated navigation, per-row action dropdowns (APG Menu Button pattern), and responsive horizontal scrolling. The primary goal is to produce a **QA-executable testing plan** that can be consistently run by rotating team members with basic accessibility knowledge, while ensuring the underlying design follows WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices Guide (APG) patterns and WCAG 2.2 AA success criteria. --- ## Semantic Structure Plan The table must use native HTML semantics to communicate structure to assistive technology without relying on ARIA for markup that already exists. ### Structure Diagram ```html
Transaction Records — 742 results
Date Description Category Amount Status Account Actions
2024-01-15 Wire Transfer Payments $1,250.00 Pending Checking #4821
Page 2 of 15
``` ### Key Semantic Decisions - **``**: Sufficient for flat, single-level column headers. **Do not** use `headers="..."` on `` elements; it is only required for complex multi-level or grouped headers (WCAG 1.3.1). - **``**: Programmatically associates the table title with the grid. Must be visible and read before the table by screen readers. - **axe-core rules to verify**: `td-headers-attr`, `th-has-data-cells`, `scope-attr-valid`, `table-duplicate-name`. --- ## Interaction Pattern Design ### 1. Sortable Column Headers - **APG Pattern:** APG Button / APG Table Pattern (https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/table/) - **Keyboard Model:** - `Tab`: Moves focus to the header cell - `Enter` or `Space`: Toggles sort direction - `Arrow Up/Down`: Navigates between rows in table mode (NVDA/JAWS) - **Programmatic Behavior:** Each click cycles `aria-sort` through: `none` → `ascending` → `descending` → `none`. ### 2. Pagination Controls - **APG Pattern:** APG Pagination / Button Pattern - **Keyboard Model:** - `Tab`: Moves focus to Previous/Next buttons or page indicator - `Enter` or `Space`: Activates button, triggers data fetch - **Programmatic Behavior:** Buttons disabled when at first/last page. Page indicator updates with live region. ### 3. Per-Row Action Menus - **APG Pattern:** APG Menu Button Pattern (https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/menu-button/) - **Keyboard Model:** - `Tab`: Moves focus to the trigger button - `Enter` or `Space`: Opens menu, focuses first item - `Arrow Down`: Moves focus down menu items - `Arrow Up`: Moves focus up menu items - `Escape`: Closes menu, restores focus to trigger button - **Programmatic Behavior:** `aria-expanded` toggles on trigger. Menu uses `role="menu"`, items use `role="menuitem"`. --- ## Focus Management Plan 1. **Table Navigation:** - Screen readers use **Table Mode** (NVDA: `Ctrl+Alt+Arrow Keys`, JAWS: `Insert+Arrow Keys`) to navigate cells. - **Browse Mode** (`B` key in NVDA) treats the table as a standard document flow; focus moves cell-by-cell via Tab. Both modes must be tested. 2. **Pagination Focus:** After page change, focus remains on the activated button (Previous/Next). This prevents unexpected jumps and aligns with WCAG 2.4.3 Focus Order. If the button becomes disabled, focus moves to the first row of the new page or a "Page X loaded" live region. 3. **Menu Focus Management:** When menu opens, focus moves to the first `menuitem`. When closed via Escape, focus returns to the trigger button. No focus trap is needed (APG Menu Button pattern uses roving tabindex/focus movement). 4. **Horizontal Scroll:** Keyboard users can scroll horizontally by focusing the table container and using `Shift+Tab` or arrow keys if implemented as a scrollable div. Ensure sticky column headers remain visible during horizontal scroll. --- ## State Communication Design | State | Visual Indicator | Programmatic Indicator | ARIA Attribute | WCAG Citation | |-------|-----------------|----------------------|-----------------|---------------| | Sort: None | No icon or neutral icon | `aria-sort="none"` on `` | `aria-sort` | WCAG 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value | | Sort: Ascending | ▲ icon | `aria-sort="ascending"` | `aria-sort` | WCAG 4.1.2 | | Sort: Descending | ▼ icon | `aria-sort="descending"` | `aria-sort` | WCAG 4.1.2 | | Menu Open | Dropdown visible, button highlighted | `aria-expanded="true"` on trigger | `aria-expanded` | WCAG 4.1.2 | | Page Change | New rows render, indicator updates | `aria-live="polite"` region updates text | `aria-live` | WCAG 4.1.3 Status Messages | | Sort Change | Live region announces "Sorted by X, ascending" | `aria-live="polite"` region content changes | `aria-live` | WCAG 4.1.3 | | Disabled Pagination | Button grayed out, cursor: not-allowed | `disabled` attribute on `

   - Skip links: Not directly relevant to table, but general page structure should have them.

   *State Communication Design:*
   - Sort state: `aria-sort` on `<th>` (none, ascending, descending).
   - Live region: `aria-live="polite"` announces sort change. Must be outside the table or carefully managed so it doesn't interrupt reading.

   - Menus: `aria-expanded` on trigger, `role="menu"`, `role="menuitem"`.

   - Column header text clarity.
